conclusion: The first 128K attempt after rebooting with MES logging reproduces the silent no-progress state before completing any prefill. Same-stream retirement stops at sequence 339 after chunk [32768,36864), while host submission reaches sequence 389 at layer 6 of [36864,40960). For 175 seconds before termination, all 36 telemetry samples remain at 100% reported activity and 2.9 GHz with median 43 W and fixed 26,662 MiB residency. A one-time gfx11 HQD snapshot finds the 1 MiB AQL compute queue active and non-empty on CP pipe 0 queue 2: rptr=0x32250, wptr=0x32450, a 0x200 hardware-pointer gap equal to 32 AQL packets with the GFX11 AQL wptr shift of 4; CP_HQD_ERROR and CP_HQD_DEQUEUE_REQUEST are zero. The 4 KiB auxiliary compute queue is active but empty with rptr=wptr=0x140. KFD fault/page counters remain zero, the kernel journal has no amdgpu/KFD fault, timeout, or reset, and gpu_recovery/send_sigterm do not fire autonomously. The raw MES event-log view is byte-identical in the healthy-active, first-stall, and +30-second snapshots, then changes after the monitor sends SIGTERM and the process exits. This proves the debug boot did not fix the failure and captures a real mapped user queue with unread work, but one HQD sample does not prove temporal pointer immobility or identify the unread packet/kernel. The MES buffer remains undecoded, and the unchanged bytes do not by themselves prove MES firmware is hung.

snapshot_order: stalled_after_30s without a second HQD dump
protocol.command: GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1 python3 scripts/qwen35_readme_sweep.py --engine gguf --model <model> --quant gguf_q4_k_m --backend hip_gfx1151 --workloads 128K/128 --warmup-runs 1 --measured-runs 3 --warmup-decode-tokens 1 --force-bulk-prefill --bulk-prefill-attention-mode bulk --use-wmma-prefill --use-gemv-decode --graph-replay-decode --compiler-version-file <precomputed> --require-cached-build --prefill-flight-recorder <out>/prefill.flight --prefill-flight-recorder-granularity layer --json <out>/result.json

boot_preflight.interpretation: Confirms the loaded parameters, cached build, model, HIP path, and short exact workload operate after reboot. It is not a 128K stability or performance baseline.

stall.termination: monitor-requested SIGTERM after all declared snapshots; no autonomous SIGTERM or GPU reset

flight_recorder.safe_interpretation: All same-stream work through chunk [32768,36864) retired. Host submission reached layer 6 of the next chunk. The pending work spans many dispatches and does not identify one kernel or packet.

kernel_journal.interpretation: The single PME line is temporally coincident but not established as trigger, cause, or GPU fault.

kfd_state.rls_all_snapshots: Node 1, gpu_id d566: No active runlist
kfd_state.rls_interpretation: Not a valid activity discriminator on this MES-managed configuration; both healthy and stalled snapshots have mapped active HQDs or advancing work despite this output.
kfd_state.mqd_caution: Mapped-queue MQDs can be stale and are not proof of hardware pointer progress.

hqd_snapshot.register_map: gfx1151/gc_11_5_0 consecutive CP registers from CP_MQD_BASE_ADDR through CP_HQD_PQ_WPTR_HI

register_map_sources.caution: AMD should confirm the mainline register map and pointer semantics against the running CachyOS kernel build.

hqd_snapshot.evidence_boundary: Only the first established-stall snapshot included HQDs. The backlog is real at that instant, but no second HQD sample exists to prove that hardware rptr/wptr were temporally frozen.

mes_event_log.interpretation: The exposed buffer records no byte change from healthy-active through both stall snapshots and does change during process teardown. This is a useful control, not proof that MES firmware stopped executing.

drm_fences.caution: amdgpu_fence_info does not expose the doorbell-driven KFD user queue. SDMA fence movement during snapshots can be caused by capture activity.

raw_mes_mqd_reads.interpretation: The debugfs MQD files did not return payloads on this kernel. The MES and MES-KIQ ring files were preserved instead.

decision.routing_reason: The symptom crosses TheRock HIP user space, ROCr/KFD, amdgpu, CP, MES firmware, and kernel hang detection. It is not established as a TheRock build/package regression. ROCm/ROCm is the stack-wide issue tracker and TheRock MES issue 2655 itself routes related gfx115x scheduler hangs to ROCm/ROCm reports.
next_steps: run one separate amdgpu.sched_policy=2 isolation boot with MES logging, preserving the same protocol, and post the result to ROCm/ROCm#6437
ask AMD for the supported MES-event decoder and a low-perturbation second-sample user-HQD/last-retired-packet method
cross-file to TheRock or drm/amd only if an AMD maintainer requests it or a future A/B establishes a tracker-specific boundary
